search_terms: assistant OR chatbot OR tutor OR memory OR personalis* OR tailor*
D1.reason_for_score: Score 2 (Activity recognised; a material boundary is unclear). N001 covers AI systems across learning and teaching and all lifecycle stages (including data collection, deployment, and decommissioning); N150 PC12 covers data captured from student digital systems for learning analytics; N121/N016/N017 cover behavioural/preference personal information and AI/automated decision-making; N010/N011 cover teaching/learning data lifecycle and disposal. However, no policy explicitly addresses course-level AI assistant memory scoping or course-end memory restriction/deletion.
D1.negative_search_or_access_note: FTS5 searches for 'memory' (in AI context), 'chatbot', 'tailor*' returned no policy rules; N136 (p.145) mentions an LMS AI assistant (Turnitin Clarity) only descriptively. N001 Section 6 AI supporting procedures are not in the corpus.

D2.reason_for_score: Score 2 (Named role, applicable criteria and decision process). Named roles hold clear decision powers: Privacy Officer oversees PIAs and privacy complaints (N011 p.233); Business Information System Owners manage access controls and CIMA decommissioning (N011 p.233); CIMA approves data deletion/destruction unless exempted (N011 p.232); CISO directs cyber security compliance (N006 p.321); and for GenAI grading/feedback pilots, the Dean (Learning and Teaching), Privacy Officer, and CIO/CISO must approve (N002 p.49). General review/complaint routes exist (N004, N121), supporting Review route = Yes, but D2 remains 2 because no explicit appeal route is directly connected to course-level AI assistant memory decisions.

D3.reason_for_score: Score 2 (Compatible rules, without explicit coordination). The AI Policy (N001), Privacy suite (N016, N017, N121), Information Management suite (N010, N011), Cyber Security suite (N005, N006), and Learning Analytics (N150 PC12) are compatible and cross-reference one another. Minor uncoordinated tensions exist without direct contradiction: N150 PC12 (2.6.1) requires prior consent for learning analytics data collection whereas N016 Appendix A permits general educational collection without separate consent; and N011/N121 subordinate deletion to WAUSDA/CIMA approval rather than course-end boundaries. Also, N016/N017/N148 (2024) still reference the pre-2026 title of N005.
D3.negative_search_or_access_note: No direct unresolved documentary contradiction found.

D4.reason_for_score: Score 2 (Usable sequence, with a relevant detail unclear). Staff have a usable governance sequence: complete the PIA checklist before system roll-out and submit to privacy@curtin.edu.au (N011 p.234, N121 p.254); complete PIA and Security Assessment for third-party/cloud storage (N017 p.245); classify, store, and seek CIMA approval before deletion unless low-value transitory (N011 pp.231-232); and students have FOI access/correction (N121 p.256) and breach/complaint routes (N213, N004). However, material details are unclear/unbundled: N001 AI procedures are missing, the PIA checklist and WAUSDA disposal schedule are not in the corpus, and there is no step-by-step process for course-end AI memory scoping or purge.
D4.negative_search_or_access_note: PIA checklist, WAUSDA Retention and Disposal Authorities, Disposal of Information guide, and N001 supporting AI procedures are not in the corpus.

D5.reason_for_score: Score 2 (Substantive protection, but a material gap remains). Substantive safeguards protect purpose/consent (N017 2.3.1, N150 2.6.1, N148 3.4.2), minimisation (N011 3.2(c), N016 3.4), security classification and storage (N011 3.3-3.4, Appendix A SENSITIVE-Personal, N005/N006, N017 2.3.3-2.3.4), and breach response (N148, N213). However, a material gap remains: no policy establishes course-scoped AI memory isolation or lawful course-end memory restriction/disposal, and N011 3.8(b) requires CIMA approval for deletion unless exempted under 3.8(c) / WAUSDA.
D5.negative_search_or_access_note: No course-end memory deletion/isolation safeguard found in N001, N011, N017, or N150. Student Privacy Collection Notice and WAUSDA are not in the corpus.

D6.reason_for_score: Score 3 (Periodic and event-triggered review, ownership and a route from monitoring to revision). N001 mandates annual review (instead of the standard 5-year cycle) or earlier if significant legislative changes occur, with assigned Policy Compliance Officer (Deputy Provost) and Policy Manager (Provost). N150 PC12 assigns two-yearly monitoring and reporting of learning analytics to the Learning and Student Experience Committee. N213 requires Information Breach Register logging with recommended mitigation measures, and N152 assigns ARCC oversight of compliance monitoring and follow-up.
D6.negative_search_or_access_note: Note: N001's scheduled 1 April - 30 June 2026 review date has passed without an updated version in the corpus.

case_summary.case_note: Curtin governs S13 (voluntary course-level AI learning assistant memory) through overlapping general frameworks rather than an AI-specific procedure: N001 (AI Policy, 2025) sets high-level principles; N016/N017/N121 (Privacy) and N010/N011 (Information Management, 2026) require purpose limitation, consent for non-primary uses, minimisation (N011 3.2(c)), PIAs/Security Assessments, SENSITIVE-Personal classification, and WAUSDA/CIMA-governed retention/disposal; N150 PC12 (Learning Analytics) requires transparency and prior consent for student digital system data; N005/N006 (Cyber Security, Sept/Oct 2026) and N148/N213 (Breach) provide security and incident response; and N121/N004/FOI provide review and complaint routes. However, under Protocol v1.1 S13 criteria, a critical gap exists because no operative instrument establishes course-scoped memory isolation or lawful course-end memory restriction/disposal (N001's supporting procedures are undeveloped/absent, and N011 3.8(b) requires CIMA approval for deletion unless exempted under 3.8(c)/WAUSDA).
